$comment: D-CSUBSET-VLA-INITIALIZER (C23 6.7.10p4) — `int a[n] = {};` is ACCEPTED and the object is really ZEROED at run time, proven by spawning the binary on every leg and in both pipeline arms. The frame is deliberately pre-filled with 0x5A5A5A5A before each probe, so a missing zero-fill cannot pass by luck. ALL THREE CHUNK ARMS of the fill are covered on purpose — the lowering picks its store width from the OBJECT'S OWN ALIGNMENT, so `double` exercises the 8-byte arm, `int` the 4-byte arm and `char` the pure-byte arm. The TAIL loop needs a case of its own, and which case is the point: for an ordinary VLA the byte total is count*elemStride and elemStride is a multiple of the element's alignment, so the total is ALWAYS a multiple of the chunk and the tail runs ZERO times. Only an OVER-ALIGNED object reaches it — `_Alignas(16) int a[3]` is 12 bytes with an 8-byte chunk, so the wide loop writes bytes 0..7 and the tail must write 8..11, i.e. exactly a[2]. Dropping the tail leaves a[2] dirty while a[0]/a[1] are clean, which is the sneakiest way this fill can fail. A multi-dimensional VLA covers the whole object rather than its first row, and a written-through VLA proves the slot is still ordinary storage afterwards. MEASURED 2026-08-25 that both references carry the same obligation: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 19.1.1 each zero the object. Red-on-disable: remove the MIR VarDecl arm's VLA interception and the empty ConstructAggregate lowers to nothing at all, so every probe reads the dirty pattern and the exit code is no longer 42 — a failure NO semantic unit test can see, which is why this example exists.
